position: Delete the user-facing tokens column now, and remove or hide the derived tps column because it is dead when tokens are absent. Do not install clients/tokens-hook.sh. Keep request_log.tokens, server aggregation, and API fields dormant rather than dropping the schema, because that is a UI-level reversible change and R5 verifies no routing reads the column. The chair's R1 measurement shows the existing transcript hook captured only 8.0% of deduped billed tokens in one real session, so it is not a cheap fix. If a real consumer later appears, rebuild on first-party OTel or an idempotent correlated update after proving accuracy and defining the metric.

claims.claim: Production tokens data is effectively empty: 11,167 requests and 13 total tokens across all hosts.
claims.evidence: Brief F3: read-only GET https://aigate.shoemoney.ai/api/stats returned the per-host table; this is a point-in-time cumulative production sample, not a rate.

claims.claim: clients/tokens-hook.sh exists but is not installed or invoked by the current client setup.
claims.evidence: Brief F2: grep -n 'tokens-hook' clients/install.sh returned nothing; ls ~/.claude/aigate/ did not show tokens-hook.sh; settings.json Stop hooks listed only aaa-selfimprove.sh and nohumans.js.

claims.claim: The current hook design appends a new request_log row with an empty prompt because no UPDATE endpoint exists.
claims.evidence: clients/tokens-hook.sh header and POST behavior; src/server.js:823 performs an unconditional INSERT for /api/events/prompt; R4b confirms the append-only producer pattern.

claims.claim: Installing the current hook unchanged would distort displayed request counts by adding extra rows per reported turn.
claims.evidence: Follows from the verified append-only hook and server INSERT path, plus /api/stats counting request_log rows; no staging measurement with the hook installed has been supplied.
claims.test: In staging, generate N known Claude Code turns with prompt-hook and tokens-hook installed, then compare request_log row count and /api/stats requests against N.

claims.claim: In the chair's measured session, last-assistant-message-only reporting captured 8.0% of deduped billed tokens.
claims.evidence: R1b: one real session, 5 user turns, 65 unique assistant messages after deduping by message.id; hook-equivalent last-only total 660,530 versus all-message billed total 8,300,849.

claims.claim: The existing last-message-only design would systematically undercount multi-message agentic turns.
claims.evidence: R1b shows capture falling to 3.1% on a 38-message turn and 100% only on a single-message turn; sample is one session, so fleet-wide systematic behavior is extrapolated.
claims.test: Repeat the deduped transcript audit across multiple tool-heavy sessions; if capture remains far below 100% for multi-message turns, systematic undercount is confirmed.

claims.claim: The installed Claude Code binary contains first-party OpenTelemetry token and cost metric identifiers.
claims.evidence: R2: strings/grep against /Users/shoemoney/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.238 found claude_code.token.usage, claude_code.cost.usage, CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY, OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER, and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT identifiers.

claims.claim: Whether Claude Code OTel output has the granularity needed for aigate dashboard rows is unknown.
claims.evidence: No runtime capture has shown session_id, host, account, model, or cost attributes sufficient for per-host/per-account dashboard rows. Experiment: run one turn with CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 and OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=console or OTLP to a local sink, then inspect emitted metrics.

claims.claim: request_log.tokens is display-only; the account-selection path does not read it.
claims.evidence: R5: full grep readout of src/server.js shows every tokens read feeds /api/logs, /api/stats, or derived tps; /api/select does not read request_log.tokens.

claims.claim: tps is derived from tokens and is equally dead in current production data.
claims.evidence: R4a: src/server.js:847 computes tps from tokens; live /api/stats by_host_1h showed tps: 0 for mbp and wick in that point-in-time window.

claims.claim: UI-only deletion of tokens and tps, while leaving schema and aggregation dormant, is the lowest-cost reversible action.
claims.evidence: R5 proves no routing dependency; R4 proves tps is dead; removal is presentation-level and git-revertible, avoiding a database migration.
claims.test: Apply the UI deletion in a branch or staging, verify dashboard rendering and API behavior, then git revert and verify restoration.

claims.claim: Deleting or clearly deprecating clients/tokens-hook.sh is safer than leaving it in clients as an apparently ready producer.
claims.evidence: R1 and R2 show the script is known-bad for the dominant workload and depends on an internal transcript format; it is not currently installed, so removal should not affect production clients.
claims.test: Remove or deprecate the script in a branch, grep install paths, run the installer in staging, and confirm no current client behavior changes.

claims.claim: Future token reporting should be rebuilt on OTel or an idempotent correlated update only after a real consumer and accurate metric definition exist.
claims.evidence: R1 disqualifies the current transcript last-message design; R2 shows a first-party telemetry path; R5 shows no current routing consumer.
claims.test: Prototype OTel ingest or PATCH correlation on one host, name an operational decision that changes because of the metric, and verify accuracy against transcript or billing data.

claims.claim: The UI comments saying tokens are architecturally always null are stale and should be removed or rewritten in the deletion commit.
claims.evidence: Brief F4: public/index.html:1081-1083 and :703-705 describe a limitation that predates the landed but undeployed Stop-hook reporter.

challenges.their_claim: Wire token reporting because token usage is the core metric for a token-budget account router and the plumbing is mostly built; fix with PATCH and all-message sums.
challenges.problem: R5 verifies the router does not read request_log.tokens, so the core-metric argument is not supported by this codebase. R1 shows the available transcript source captures only 8.0% of measured billed tokens, and PATCH would fix row duplication but not undercount, transcript instability, or the undefined composite metric.
challenges.test: Show a concrete selection or operator decision that changes because of this per-host token number, and demonstrate a staging reporter that captures near-complete usage for tool-heavy turns without corrupting request counts.

challenges.their_claim: Redesign and wire if the controlled multi-message experiment leaves room; otherwise deletion is safer.
challenges.problem: The experiment has been run and the result is adverse: last-only capture was 8.0% in the measured session, with 3.1% on the largest agentic turn. That removes the conditional basis for redesigning the existing transcript hook.
challenges.test: Supply a different source, such as a verified OTel capture or an all-message correlated reporter, that demonstrates accurate usage and a defined metric; without that, deletion is safer.

challenges.their_claim: The remaining gap may be worth closing: wire the existing machinery or delete the column.
challenges.problem: The remaining gap is not a small wire. The available producer appends rows, corrupts a displayed metric, parses an internal format, fails open into silent zeroes, and reports a composite number whose meaning is not defined. R5 also shows no product behavior depends on the column.
challenges.test: Name a consumer and run a staging comparison showing accurate, non-corrupting telemetry; if no consumer or accurate producer exists, delete the UI column.

retractions.was: If a cheap local experiment later proves Stop usage is cumulative and we add an idempotent update/correlation endpoint, we can re-add the column.
retractions.now: The experiment did not prove cumulative usage; it showed last-message-only capture of 8.0% of billed tokens, so re-adding the column via the existing transcript hook is not viable.
retractions.because: Chair-supplied R1 measurement resolved U1/U2/C5 against the existing hook.

retractions.was: Whether the last assistant usage block is cumulative for a turn is UNMEASURED.
retractions.now: It has been measured as inadequate for this purpose: last-only is far below the deduped all-message sum in the tested session.
retractions.because: R1b chair-verified transcript audit with 5 turns and 65 unique assistant messages.

retractions.was: Leaving clients/tokens-hook.sh dormant preserves option value with little risk.
retractions.now: Leaving it in clients is a footgun; it should be deleted from the active client path or clearly deprecated because it is known to undercount heavily and depends on unstable internals.
retractions.because: R1 and R2 supplied by the chair show the script is not merely unfinished but misleading.

retractions.was: Request double-counting from the hook was an untested theory.
retractions.now: The append mechanism is established by code and R4b; I still treat fleet-scale magnitude as staging-testable, but the failure shape is real enough to disqualify installing the hook unchanged.
retractions.because: Chair-supplied R4b and src/server.js citations confirmed unconditional INSERT per POST and multiple producers.

needs_research: What runtime attributes and granularity does Claude Code OTel actually emit, and does it include session, host, account, model, or cost labels usable by aigate?
What concrete fleet decision or dashboard consumer would use per-host or per-account token totals that is not already served by the account poller's limits and reset windows?
Do any non-dashboard API consumers depend on /api/stats tokens or tps fields if we later remove them from the API as well as the UI?
What is the provenance of the 13 historical production token rows, and should they be marked legacy if any future token metric is introduced?
